decisions.reason: As a design-led decorative fabric very close to existing know-how it was easy to launch, but its fashion-sensitive and overlapping nature makes it more likely to be replaced once the firm has learned which variants customers actually reorder.

The firm can readily understand and market this transparent burnout fabric through its existing textile and sampling capabilities, yet its niche decorative role and overlap with related burnout lines raise the chance of assortment pruning.

Because this product draws on established decorative-fabric knowledge the firm can absorb market feedback well, but as another closely related burnout article it faces a meaningful risk of being dropped in a collection clean-up.

A velour-like upholstery fabric fits strongly with the firm’s core upholstery offer, stocked-service model, and customer base, so existing knowledge should support refinement and continued commercialization.

This flame-retardant inbetween fabric builds on the firm’s current textile capabilities while adding a functional feature valued by buyers, making it a product the firm can learn from and sustain despite some portfolio risk.

The lining fabric is closely related to the firm’s sewing, sampling, and broad-assortment strengths, so it is relatively easy to absorb into the range and support commercially even if it is not a standout innovation.
